analysis.one_liner: TVS Motor makes and sells two-wheelers, three-wheelers and electric two-wheelers in India and over 80 export markets, with an in-house NBFC (TVS Credit) that finances a large chunk of its retail sales.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) volumes were strong: total sales up 27% to roughly 1.9 million units, with electric two-wheeler sales up 133% YoY to 186,000 units and exports up 35%. The company also launched an updated TVS Radeon commuter motorcycle for the festive season and flagged a Hyundai-TVS electric mini-truck aimed at a 2027 launch. The trading window closed on 1 October ahead of full Q2 FY27 financial results, due 14 November 2026 - about four weeks from today, so not immediate.
analysis.plain_terms: TVS is one of India's largest two-wheeler makers, and it's riding two growth waves at once - a broad festive-season volume recovery and rapid EV adoption (EV volumes more than doubled in the latest quarter). The tension: the stock already prices in a lot of this, trading near 54 times earnings, well above where a bike maker historically trades. There's also a reporting quirk worth knowing - TVS Motor's consolidated balance sheet includes TVS Credit, its own lending arm that finances customer purchases, so the group's debt ratios look far more leveraged than the actual motorcycle-making business. Judge the manufacturing business and the financing business separately.
analysis.quarters: Q3 FY26 (Dec 2025): consolidated PAT up 49% YoY to ₹841 cr on revenue of ₹14,756 cr, EBITDA margin 13.1%. Q4 FY26 (Mar 2026): revenue up 30% YoY to ₹15,053 cr, PAT up 19% to ₹771.5 cr, but EBITDA margin actually fell YoY, from 13.96% to 13.11% - margin went backward even as revenue grew, a sign costs rose faster than price/mix that quarter. Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026): record quarter - revenue up 38% YoY to ₹13,896 cr, EBITDA up 41% to ₹1,779 cr, margin recovered to 12.8% (from 12.5% a year earlier), PAT up 51% to ₹1,174 cr. Q2 FY27 volumes (pre-financials) grew 27%, with EV 2W up 133% and exports up 35%; full P&L lands 14 November 2026. Net: revenue and profit growth have been consistently strong, but the margin line has swung both ways quarter to quarter rather than expanding cleanly - worth watching whether Q2 FY27 confirms margin improvement or repeats the Q4 FY26 dip.
analysis.performance_read: No demerger or spin-off sits in this stock's history - only two forward stock splits (10:1 in 2003, 2:1 in 2010), both of which are standard adjustments baked into the return series shown, so there is no understated-returns issue here to correct for. On that basis, the long-run numbers are genuinely strong: the stock is up 615% over 5 years versus Nifty's 25% and peer Bajaj Auto's 198%, and up 157% over 3 years versus Nifty's 17% and peer's 112%. Nearer term it has cooled: over 1 year TVS is up 14.9%, roughly in line with Bajaj Auto's 15.3% and well ahead of a falling Nifty, while the stock sits 8.3% below its 10 August 2026 peak of ₹4,466 - a normal pullback after a sharp run, not a crash.
analysis.valuation_read: Expensive, and for a reason the market can point to: TVS trades around 54x trailing earnings, a roughly 7% premium to the two-wheeler peer median, but the price-to-book premium is far starker at about 17x versus a peer median near 7x (a 135% premium). The P/E gap is modest; the P/B gap is not. That gap is explained by TVS's unusually high ROE (~33-35%, versus a peer median near 21%) - a mix of strong brand economics and leverage from the TVS Credit financing book - rather than by ROCE, which at ~17-18% is actually below the peer median of ~21%. Whether that premium is justified depends entirely on whether the current EV and export growth rates hold; it is not cheap by any conventional measure.
analysis.growth_read: Mostly volume-led right now. Revenue growth of 30-38% YoY over the last three quarters has tracked closely with unit volume growth (27% in Q2 FY27, with EV units up 133%), while EBITDA margin has moved in a narrow 12.8%-13.96% band and actually fell YoY in Q4 FY26 before recovering in Q1 FY27. That is a healthier growth mix than a pure price-hike story, but it also means the premium valuation is betting on volumes (especially EV share gains) continuing, not on margins structurally re-rating higher.
analysis.health_read: On the numbers available, profit growth has tracked EBITDA growth closely (EBITDA +41% YoY, PAT +51% YoY in Q1 FY27), suggesting earnings are translating into real operating cash rather than being an accounting artifact. The headline concern is a consolidated debt-to-equity of about 3.4x - but this consolidates TVS Credit, the group's NBFC lending arm, whose borrowings fund customer loans rather than the motorcycle business itself. The core manufacturing business's standalone net debt is understood to run much lower (rating agencies reference it separately), but the exact standalone figure is Not verified - check on Screener. The more relevant risk is business risk - can EV and export momentum continue - rather than balance-sheet distress in the auto business; the main unverified question is the asset quality of TVS Credit's rapidly growing loan book.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding (the TVS family/TVS Holdings group) has been flat at 50.27% for five straight quarters (Jun'25 through Jun'26), with zero pledged shares reported as of June 2026 - a clean, stable promoter position. FII and DII holding percentages are reported inconsistently across sources (one shows roughly 20% FII / 21% DII, another shows single-digit FII with a much larger 'public' bucket), so the precise institutional split is Not verified - check on Screener; treat the promoter and pledge figures as the reliable part of this picture. No widely-tracked individual marquee investor was identified on the register in the sources checked.
strengths: Record Q1 FY27 quarter: revenue ₹13,896 cr (+38% YoY), EBITDA ₹1,779 cr (+41% YoY), PAT ₹1,174 cr (+51% YoY)
EV two-wheeler volumes up 133% YoY in Q2 FY27 to 186,000 units - clear share gains in the fastest-growing segment
Promoter holding steady at 50.27% for five consecutive quarters with zero pledged shares
Export volumes up 35% YoY in Q2 FY27, reducing reliance on the domestic cycle alone
watchpoints: Valuation is stretched on both counts - P/E ~54x (7% above peer median) and P/B ~17x (135% above peer median)
EBITDA margin fell YoY in Q4 FY26 (13.96% to 13.11%) before recovering in Q1 FY27 - the margin trend has not been one-directional
Consolidated debt-to-equity of 3.43x is inflated by the TVS Credit NBFC book; the standalone auto-business leverage and TVS Credit's loan-book asset quality are not independently verified here
Stock is 8.3% below its 10 August 2026 peak - near-term momentum has cooled even though the multi-year trend remains strongly positive
analysis.one_thing: The 14 November 2026 Q2 FY27 results - specifically whether EBITDA margin resumes clear expansion (as in Q1 FY27) rather than repeating the YoY dip seen in Q4 FY26, which would confirm the current 27% volume growth is margin-accretive and not just volume-led.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly P&L (Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27) cross-checked across company press release and multiple financial news outlets with consistent figures. Valuation ratios (P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE) cross-checked across two independent sources with close but not identical values; ranges given reflect that. Promoter holding and zero-pledge status consistent across sources. FII/DII shareholding split conflicted across sources and is flagged as unverified rather than averaged. Standalone (ex-NBFC) net debt figure for the core auto business could not be verified and should be checked on Screener.
